claims.claim: The game features a massive passive skill tree and deep character customization mechanics that require external guides or extensive research to understand.

citations.review_text:
I want to like this game. I want so very, very badly to like this game. But I can't. This is easily the most complex ARPG I've ever played, and I've played a lot, and as a consequence of that and certain design decisions, this game is outrageously hostile to casual blind playthroughs. To clarify what I mean by this, I mean playthroughs where you pick up the game knowing little to nothing about it and do a quick playthrough of the campaign and maybe a little endgame. That's usually what I want out of ARPGs, as I usually find endgame content in ARPGs to be mind-numbingly boring and I'm not super fond of replaying ARPGs to try different classes. So I'm not here to judge POE's endgame, not that I've reached it anyway.

What I am here to judge is the campaign playthrough. The actual campaign, from what I've played, is honestly pretty solid. The issue is the mechanical density of actually playing the game. Everyone knows about the skill tree. The thing is ridiculous, far too large to truly be able to parse and craft a decent build out of without many, many hours of playtime fiddling with it. I would be okay with this, except respeccing without already having a good build to farm currency is sufficiently expensive to be basically impossible. Compare this with, say, Grim Dawn, where unless you're undoing every single skill point, it's viable to respec. Or, Diablo 3 and 4, where respeccing your skills is completely free and can be done at any time outside of combat. This gives a high level of flexibility to try out builds, and if they don't work, you can change them immediately. That just isn't really possible in POE.

Add on to that the relatively high level of difficulty, especially if you don't know about the need to stack resistances, and you can very easily build yourself into a corner where your only viable option to fix things is to start a new character. I hate starting new characters. There's no reason why the game has to make respeccing expensive, or even limited a…
Fun but very confusing as a new player

Extremely repetitive and boring gameplay (which is laggy AF) makes for a miserable experience all around.

Can't be played without a guide and extensive research which is also lame.
Difficult to follow without help from youtube but very fun once you learn even half the mechanics

Recommended 💎⚔️

Path of Exile isn't just an action RPG—it's a hobby disguised as a free game.

The amount of character customization is incredible. Between the massive passive skill tree, Ascendancy classes, support gems, crafting, and countless unique items, every build feels like a new adventure. Experimenting with different combinations is just as fun as fighting monsters. 🌳✨

Combat is fast, satisfying, and becomes wonderfully chaotic in the endgame. Clearing entire screens of enemies, hunting for valuable loot, and constantly improving your gear creates one of the most addictive gameplay loops in the genre. 💥💰

The leagues keep the game feeling fresh by introducing new mechanics and challenges every few months. Combined with the deep Atlas endgame, trading, and boss fights, there's always another goal to chase. 🗺️👹

The learning curve is brutal. New players will probably spend almost as much time reading guides as playing, and inventory management can be frustrating without extra stash tabs. But once everything clicks, it's incredibly rewarding. 📚😅

I logged in to try a new build. A few hours later I had 15 browser tabs open, three crafting calculators, and absolutely no regrets. 😂♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥to play. Dangerous to your free time. 💀

Path of Exile features an enormous passive skill tree, deep item crafting, seasonal challenge leagues, a vast endgame Atlas system, and extensive character customization, making it one of the deepest ARPGs available.

claims.claim: High-level crafting relies heavily on random number generation and consumes consumables without clear in-game explanations of how the systems work.

Great dungeon crawler - I'm optimized for graphics, at least so I think and i love the diversity of enemies and playable characters.  Microtransactions enable different looks, as opposed to the in-game armor making you look cool - so that leaves much to be desired and it is not cheap.  Expect a game that requires good inventory management.  I like the crafting system generally, but high level is RNG based.
There is much in the game that is not explained, like how crafting works, given that crafting requires consumables, it would be good if that were a bit clearer in my humble opinion, otherwise it leads to just hording your mats and not wanting to waste them on testing.  I love the community, especially the loot filters by devs - makes the game much more playable and not all too intense in clearing out inventory.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that purchasing stash tabs is virtually mandatory to comfortably play the endgame and manage items effectively.

citations.review_text:
Hands down one of the best ARPGs of all time, PoE delivers almost everything an ARPG fan wants, and it doesn't charge you $70 upfront to find out.

Path of Exile’s Atlas mapping system offers over 100 maps, dozens of endgame bosses, and layers of mechanics that you can customize to play exactly the content you want. The massive passive skill tree and flexible skill gem system give you the freedom to make almost any crazy build work.
You can play PoE’s entire campaign and endgame for free. The only [b]"mandatory"[/b] purchase to comfortably play the endgame is a few stash tabs, which is a fraction of the cost of D4’s base game and seasonal passes.

Another thing I love is the studio itself, GGG routinely sits down for Q&As with community members and streamers. When the community points out that a mechanic feels terrible or that mobs don't feel as rewarding as they should be, GGG responds quickly with lists of balance updates and QoL fixes based directly on player feedback. They aren't afraid to admit when they've made a mistake or when they aren't happy with the current state of the game. They also deliberately try to avoid mid league nerfs to respect the time players have invested in their builds.

Path of Exile has been a staple of the ARPG scene since its release, through good expansions and bad, its had a large player base and the most complicated skill tree I have ever seen. From casual play to die hard gamers, it features enough content to keep you occupied for days on end. 

Also its a free game, no real pay to win, but without more stash tabs, you might be struggle bussing a little bit.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign and map progression feature sudden, untelegraphed one-shot deaths from off-screen or from visually cluttered encounters without a death log.

citations.review_text:
Welp, after a years-long break I can say that this game is fundamentally broken with power creep and content bloat. The balancing team must have (understandably) given up leagues ago. Most of the time you have no way of knowing what is actually dangerous on your screen at any time - a random magic mob can one-shot you from off-screen with an autoattack while bosses barely dent your health. And if you have a visually busy build, just hope that you have enough damage to ignore game mechanics.

In the end, you either break the game or see how truly broken it is.

Really gave this game a good try but once campaign ended, what to do felt overwhelming. The content doesn't feel intuitive or cohesive. Feels like a bunch of mini games thrown into one game, with no indication on where to start or what each one is good for, or how to "play" them.

and I tried just chipping away piece by piece, and not sure if I learned much.

But what really killed the game for me is how content goes from blasting along, to getting one shot without any real clear animation, or telegraphed effect, or way to change the UI to put debuffs not off to the side of the screen, etc. There isn't a death log either. 

I think this game would have been great if you learned and grew as it developed but coming in as a new player now is challenging in an unfun way.
